implementation_notes: MockK's spyk(Car()) wraps a copy of a real object: calls run the real implementation and are recorded, then verify { car.drive(Direction.NORTH) } and confirmVerified(car) assert the interactions, with @SpyK wiring the same into annotation-based tests alongside @InjectMockKs. What replaces the classic spy is the MockK proxy over the real instance - note that the spy is a copy of the passed object, so state assigned after spyk() is not visible to it.
pitfalls: The spy holds a copy of the constructor state: mutations made on the original after spyk() are invisible - construct the object after its state is final.
Using a spy with a suspending function gives unexpected results (known issue #554); prefer coVerify and verify the coroutine view deliberately.
Spies and mockkStatic may fail on JDK 16+ where reflective access is restricted, and inline functions or final constructs cannot be mocked at all.
